narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your total years of professional experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and the fact that you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter careers (1–5 years is most common among stayers), your mid-level experience aligns more with people who begin exploring new opportunities. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in your current organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction. This tenure is actually typical among stayers, but combined with your broader career stage it signals readiness for change. Finally, receiving external job offers was a clear factor pulling the prediction toward departure. Most employees who stay never receive such offers, so this strongly suggested you have attractive alternatives.

Taken together, these elements created a picture of someone likely to move on. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You may want to reflect on whether the right internal opportunities could change your plans, while the company could explore ways to better retain experienced talent like you.
